subject: geography
title: Population distribution and density
objective: Distinguish distribution from density and explain where people live.

lesson.opening: People are spread unevenly across the planet. Distribution is where they are; density is how many per area.

sections.heading: Density versus distribution
sections.body: Density divides population by area. Distribution describes the pattern — clustered, scattered, or along a coast or river.

sections.heading: Where people live
sections.body: People tend to live where climate is mild, water is available, soils are fertile, and jobs exist. Extreme cold, deserts, and high mountains are sparsely populated.

sections.heading: The uneven map
sections.body: Most of the world’s people live on a small share of the land, often near coasts and plains.

activities.prompt: Which area is usually sparsely populated?
Which is a common reason people cluster near coasts?
Explain why population is unevenly distributed.
activities.context: Climate, water, soil, relief, and jobs pull people toward some places and push them from others.
